chapter: Sidney Bechet and the Paris festival
title: Central Plaza, Stuyvesant Casino and Lou Terassi's
summary: Moore played with Bechet and in Dixieland sessions at New York clubs with Red Allen, Buster Bailey, Willie the Lion and others.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Now, with Bechet, now, you were with him two different times it seems -- 1947 after the Armstrong band broke up until 1949 and then back again in 1951 or were you straight through with him from about '47 to '51, and where did you tour with Bechet?

Well, during that time, I was on and off with Bechet different times on 52nd Street and then when he would leave the place, he'd rather go by himself to Europe or to another location. He didn't take me along because I had something else to do and in that way I got to play the Central Plaza with quite a number of other people like Willie "the Lion" (Smith) and Red Allen and Buster Bailey and Fletcher Henderson and Max Kaminsky and Bill Davison, Pete Johnson, and a lot of the guys, Tony Parenti was there and Conrad Janis was there, too. This is the Central Plaza group and for a while I worked across the street at the Stuesant Casino for Bob Moss and practically the same group would go over there and the same musicians that had played with Bob Monse would come over to Central Plaza and play over there for a while. And in that way -- that year, New York was jumping.
Then at one time there was a place called

Lou Terassi's on 47th Street towards 8th Avenue. I played there with Red Allen and I think Buster Bailey was on that too. And also the other trombone player, Vic Dickinson, Benny Morton --
Dickie Wells, he was there, too, once in a while. It provided work for practically every musician around New York.
